correctness.rationale: Exact Dirichlet first and second moments yield the CV identity. Uniform gamma-ratio expansion for alpha=O(log N) and Stirling prove the logarithmic L2 crossover. The normalized iid-exponential representation reduces the probability laws to sums of exponential powers: fixed-ratio subcritical law follows by second moment or truncation, supercritical collapse by a maximum bound and tilted gamma lower tail, and the sqrt(log N) boundary by a shrinking relative cutoff window and a gamma CLT. The truncated-variance bound follows from monotonicity of u^(2alpha)e^(-u). Constants and normalizations were separately recomputed; 597 finite exact/numeric checks passed. All infinite statements are proved analytically rather than inferred from experiments.

value.rationale: The source motivates tuning the Fermat exponent against sampling variability. The theorem gives two exact sample-size-dependent logarithmic scales, a half-log-log correction with a limiting variance constant, a full normal-CDF boundary for typical normalized distances, and a nonuniform-integrability regime where relative variance diverges despite concentration in probability. These distinctions change the interpretation of the standard coefficient-of-variation diagnostic in a natural finite-sample geometric statistic, and are more than routine fixed-parameter substitutions.
